featuredPapers.title: Supraglottic Airway versus Bag-Valve-Mask Ventilation in Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: A Pragmatic Randomized Trial
featuredPapers.summary: Multicentre RCT (n=4,210) finding no difference in 30-day survival between initial SGA insertion and BVM ventilation, but SGA resulted in fewer airway complications and faster time to first ventilation.
featuredPapers.relevance: 🟢 High — direct prehospital airway management evidence
featuredPapers.featuredReason: Landmark trial directly comparing two foundational airway strategies in OHCA — changes to guidelines likely

featuredPapers.title: Tranexamic Acid in Paediatric Traumatic Brain Injury: Prehospital Administration Feasibility Study
featuredPapers.summary: Prospective cohort across 8 EMS agencies demonstrating safe prehospital TXA administration in children with suspected TBI, with 94% protocol compliance and no adverse thromboembolic events.
featuredPapers.relevance: 🟢 High — extends TXA evidence to paediatric prehospital population
featuredPapers.featuredReason: First prehospital paediatric TXA feasibility data — addresses a significant evidence gap

featuredPapers.title: Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation in Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
featuredPapers.summary: Meta-analysis of 14 studies (n=62,500) showing ECPR associated with improved survival to hospital discharge (OR 2.8, 95% CI 1.9-4.1) in refractory VF/VT arrest when initiated within 60 minutes.
featuredPapers.relevance: 🟢 High — ECPR evidence synthesis relevant to advanced EMS systems
featuredPapers.featuredReason: Comprehensive meta-analysis strengthening the case for ECPR in selected patients — important for services considering implementation

featuredPapers.title: Ketamine versus Midazolam for Excited Delirium Syndrome in the Prehospital Setting
featuredPapers.summary: Retrospective cohort (n=892) showing ketamine was associated with faster sedation onset and fewer required rescue doses compared to midazolam, but higher rates of emergent airway intervention (12% vs 5%).
featuredPapers.relevance: 🟡 Medium — relevant to operational chemical sedation protocols
featuredPapers.featuredReason: Directly informs the ketamine vs midazolam debate for excited delirium — safety signal worth noting

papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine

papers.title: Inhaled Methoxyflurane for Acute Traumatic Pain in the Prehospital Setting: A Randomized Controlled Trial
papers.summary: RCT (n=312) demonstrating inhaled methoxyflurane provided clinically significant pain reduction (≥2 points on NRS) within 5 minutes, with efficacy comparable to IV fentanyl but without requiring IV access.

papers.title: Accuracy of SALT Triage among Paramedics in Simulated Mass Casualty Incidents
papers.summary: Simulation-based study finding SALT triage accuracy of 71% among experienced paramedics, with consistent under-triage of respiratory compromise and over-triage of walking wounded.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium — triage training implications for MCI preparedness

papers.title: Standard versus High-Dose Epinephrine in Pediatric Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest
papers.summary: Retrospective analysis of 1,847 paediatric OHCA cases finding no survival benefit with high-dose epinephrine (0.1 mg/kg) over standard dose (0.01 mg/kg), and increased risk of post-ROSC myocardial dysfunction.
papers.relevance: 🔴 Indirect — paediatric cardiac arrest, reinforces current dosing recommendations

papers.title: Ventilated versus Non-Ventilated Chest Seals for Penetrating Thoracic Trauma: A Swine Model
papers.journal: Journal of Trauma and Acute Care Surgery
papers.summary: Animal model study (n=30) demonstrating that ventilated chest seals significantly reduced tension pneumothorax development compared to non-ventilated seals in penetrating thoracic trauma with positive-pressure ventilation.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High — directly informs chest seal selection in paramedic protocols

papers.title: Impact of 12-Hour versus 24-Hour Shifts on Paramedic Cognitive Performance: A Longitudinal Cohort Study
papers.summary: Prospective cohort (n=184 paramedics) showing significant declines in clinical decision-making accuracy and reaction time in the final 4 hours of 24-hour shifts, with no such decline on 12-hour shifts.
papers.relevance: 🟡 Medium — workforce and safety implications for EMS scheduling

papers.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Paramedic-Performed Point-of-Care Ultrasound for Abdominal Free Fluid
papers.summary: Prospective diagnostic accuracy study with trained paramedic sonographers achieving 87% sensitivity and 93% specificity for abdominal free fluid detection after a 16-hour focused training programme.
papers.relevance: 🟢 High — emerging paramedic skill with demonstrated diagnostic accuracy
